args.title: Only treat a quote as a CSV delimiter at the start of a field
args.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

splitFields currently enters quoted mode whenever it sees a `"` anywhere in the line, so an inch mark inside an unquoted description (e.g. `Monitor 27" Dell U2724D`) is treated as opening a quoted field and swallows the rest of the line, including the real commas. Change splitFields to only treat a `"` as starting a quoted field when it appears at the very start of a field (i.e. `current === ""` and not already inQuotes); a `"` appearing elsewhere in an unquoted field should be kept as a literal character. This matches standard CSV quoting rules and fixes rows like the one in the issue without affecting properly quoted fields.

splitFields toggles quoted mode on any `"` it sees, even mid-field, so an inch mark like `27"` in an unquoted description is read as opening a quoted field and swallows the rest of the line's commas, producing the column-count mismatch. The fix is to only enter quoted mode when the `"` starts a field (current field so far is empty and not already inQuotes), leaving a `"` elsewhere in an unquoted field as a literal character. Opened a draft PR with this approach rather than merging #952 directly, since I haven't verified that PR's diff, but the fix should be equivalent in spirit.
